text:
Filip Hronek plays more than anyone on a Canucks team that has very little to show for it. He's at 26 minutes a night, with 13 points in 19 games (eight on the power play), and on Saturday in Edmonton he reached 300 career points. On a team with seven points in the standings, he's one of the reasons the power play functions at all.

The five-on-five picture is harder. Vancouver has taken just 38% of the expected goals with him on the ice. Some of that is the company: Evolving-Hockey's numbers last season had his teammates in the bottom 6% by impact, which makes his raw numbers look worse than his own effect. He was worth 1.6 wins by their measure, 41st among defensemen, mostly on the power play.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says his offense lives in transition: a quarter of his shots come off the rush. Our range projects 44 to 66 points over a full season. Whatever the Canucks decide to become this year, Hronek is the kind of minutes-eater either version needs.
headline: Hronek carries the load in Vancouver
